posts.text: pirate chain just discovered the ultimate blockchain feature: ctrl + z. An attacker exploited two validation flaws to create 39.82 million fake ARRR, temporarily inflating the supply by around 20%. The community approved a chain rollback to block 4,176,944, and the team has released mandatory upgrade v6.0.14 to remove the counterfeit coins and restore supply integrity. posts.text: $586M LOCKED BEHIND A PASSWORD. In 2011, programmer Stefan Thomas received 7,002 BTC from a Bitcoin enthusiast as payment for creating an educational video called “What Is Bitcoin?” At $83,700 per BTC, that payment is now worth $586.1 million. The catch? He stored his wallet’s private keys on an encrypted IronKey USB drive, lost the password, and has only 2 attempts left after 8 failed guesses. Cybersecurity firm Unciphered later claimed it could crack a similar device, but Thomas’s Bitcoin remains inaccessible. Imagine making an educational video and accidentally earning the hardest money in the world to recover. Would you risk the final two guesses?

posts.text: Japan might let tourists get their tax refunds in stablecoins. Japan is exploring stablecoins for its tourist consumption-tax refund system as it prepares to switch to a refund-based model on November 1. Under the new system, visitors pay tax-inclusive prices first, then claim a refund after customs checks when leaving Japan within 90 days of purchase. If stablecoins become part of the process, getting your tax refund could eventually feel less like paperwork and more like receiving a crypto transfer. Imagine shopping in Tokyo, leaving Japan, and getting your tax refund straight into your wallet. Would you take your refund in stablecoins instead of yen?
